narrative: The assessment estimates a 69% chance that you will leave your job. Because that is a high retention risk, the organization has denied the promotion at this time. The strongest factor in the estimate was your total work experience of one to five years, which worked in your favor by making leaving less likely; this is also the most common experience band among employees predicted to stay, at about half. The next most important factor was that you have received other job opportunities. Only about one in four employees predicted to stay had such opportunities, so this raised your predicted chance of leaving. The third factor was working in a sector classified as “other.” Since about one in five employees predicted to stay work in that sector, this also nudged the estimate toward leaving. Although your experience level was the single most influential factor and pointed toward staying, the two next most important factors both pointed toward leaving, and the overall estimate remained high. The organization should discuss your career path, promotion criteria, and retention concerns openly, and consider whether additional support, recognition, or development could reduce your likelihood of leaving. You may also want to clarify what would make you stay and what opportunities you are considering, so both sides can make an informed decision.
